kai: hey folks, just joined and trying the quickstart. i generated a key but calls return 429 very quickly. i'm only doing a few small requests though. any ideas?

devex-zoe: welcome! :wave: two quick checks: 1) are you using the sandbox key or a hosted key? sandbox has lower default quotas. 2) check if your code is retrying in a tight loop and causing a spike. can you paste (redact key) the response headers?

kai: using the sandbox key from Console > API Keys. response includes: "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests" and header "x-rate-limit: 40"

ops-bot: Notice: New account sandbox defaults -> 40 req/min, 50k tokens/day. Temporary bursts may be throttled. See Console -> Usage for details.

mike (infra): that x-rate-limit header is our short form for quotas. Check x-rate-limit-remaining and x-rate-limit-reset too. If remaining hits 0 you'll see 429 until reset. Also some SDKs auto-batch; verify your client isn't sending multiple requests concurrently per action.

kai: i dont see x-rate-limit-remaining in the response, only x-rate-limit and x-request-id. why would that be missing?

devex-zoe: if you hit a global token quota (daily), we sometimes return a generic 429 without remaining. open Console -> Usage -> Keys -> select the key and it will show token/day usage.

tara (security): small note: sandbox keys should still never be committed. If you rotated a key in Git history, rotate again and run git-secrets scan.

kai: ah i was running tests in parallel 20 workers which explains it. i'll throttle and re-run. is there a recommended per-second pacing?

mike (infra): aim for <= 1 request/sec per worker for sandbox if each request is multi-token. For sustained load use a hosted/prod key or request a higher sandbox quota via Support -> Quota Request with expected token counts.

kai: thanks! one more: how long do sandbox keys live? do they expire?

devex-zoe: they don't auto-expire, but you can rotate or revoke anytime in Console. for demo creds we sometimes create short-lived tokens via the API keys page.

kai: perfect, that solves it. appreciate the quick help :pray:

ops-bot: Tip: set up alerting on Console -> Usage -> Alerts to notify you before hitting daily token limits.

kai: will do!
